raw_response:
I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. At 58, I know this soil and this climate well. Hebei's North China Plain is wheat-maize country — that rotation has fed my family and paid my bills for thirty years. I'm not switching.

My biggest worry this year, same as every year, is water. The groundwater table here keeps dropping. My neighbors who over-irrigate are slowly killing the aquifer we all depend on. I've read the extension bulletins — I understand what's happening — so I irrigate carefully. Three passes on the wheat, one on the maize if summer rain cooperates.

I'll plant all 15 mu in winter wheat this October, then follow with summer maize on the same ground after the June harvest. I buy improved wheat seed — Jimai 22 has been reliable for me — and hybrid maize seed, Zhengdan 958. The hybrid costs more but the yield difference justifies it every time.

Fertilizer: I've learned to split my nitrogen applications rather than dumping it all at sowing. Reduces runoff, and the plants take it up better at jointing. I keep phosphorus and potassium at maintenance levels — my soil tests don't show deficiencies.

No-tillage on the maize. After wheat harvest I direct-seed straight into the stubble. Saves time, saves fuel, holds moisture.
